summary: Big Ridge, Tioga County: 1914 tree observation post set 40 feet up, used to about 1917, no longer standing. Thin record; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: Tree tower: a tree observation post set 40 feet above the ground
facts.status_note: The register says it is no longer standing.

events.note: Tree observation post set 40 feet above the ground (Eastern US Lookouts); the register also gives 1914 for the tree tower
Register says the tree tower was still used around 1917

evidence.supports: The 1914 tree observation post was set 40 feet above the ground
evidence.quote: 1914: A tree observation post established at 40 feet above the ground.

evidence.supports: The register dates the tree tower to 1914, used around 1917, and says it is no longer standing
evidence.quote: This tree tower was built in 1914 and still used circa 1917. It is no longer standing.

evidence.supports: A gazetteer places a 1,850-foot Big Ridge in Tioga County near the Bradley Wales Picnic Area

evidence.quote: Big Ridge is situated nearby to Bradley Wales Picnic Area, as well as near the hamlet Tiadaghton

evidence.supports: Leetonia lies about 3 miles southwest of Big Ridge
evidence.quote: Leetonia is situated 3 miles southwest of Big Ridge.

evidence.supports: Leetonia lies in the Tioga State Forest
evidence.quote: It lies along Leetonia Road, in the Tioga State Forest between Pennsylvania Route 414 and U.S. Route 6.

notes_for_editor: Thin record: two sources give one line each about the tower, and they agree on 1914 and the tree form. The height_m value is the 40-foot platform figure converted to metres. Mapcarta is a gazetteer, used only for location context; it does not place the tower on a particular spot. Do not confuse with the Big Ridge Fire Tower built in 1935 at Lost River State Park, West Virginia, which surfaced in search and is a different structure. The Eastern page's 1928 Tioga district tower on Buck Run Mountain is also a different tower. No photos found.
